newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases controls on firms' overseas investment.
newsitem.headline: India eases controls on firms' overseas investment.

text.p: The government on Friday announced the easing of restrictions on overseas investment by Indian companies.
The new measures were designed to encourage Indian firms to expand overseas and help the country move towards capital account convertibility of the rupee, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.

The ministry said Indian companies raising funds through Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs), or equity offerings overseas, could now mobilise up to 50 percent of the value of the offering through investment in foreign ventures.
It did not say what the earlier, lower investment limit was.

The Reserve Bank of India, the country's central bank, which was earlier authorised to approve Indian firms' investment proposals valued at up to $10 million, can now clear plans for up to $15 million, the ministry said.
